The ACA's Medicaid expansion is a classic case of good intentions derailed by bureaucratic bloat. While expanding coverage sounds noble, the program's $88 billion in improper payments last year alone proves systemic failure. 

H.R. 111 offers a smarter path by letting Americans deduct health insurance premiums directly—putting choice in patients' hands, not D.C. bureaucrats. The Department of Education already axed $881 million in wasteful healthcare contracts that did nothing for care quality. 

Real reform means empowering individuals, not expanding broken systems where 1,500 millionaires collected Medicaid benefits illegally. Until we stop subsidizing inefficiency, no amount of funding increases will fix healthcare's core problem: government middlemen skimming billions while patients get crumbs.
